column1: # THE TIMING ROWS (2026-09-30): what a 10-month moving-average exit does on the record's month-end
# closes, and the market's own one-year trend; the record's reading of `timing_of_monthly` /
# `timingOfMonthly`. At each month's end the rule is in equity for the next month when the
# level is above the mean of the last ten month-end levels, this one included, else out; fully
# sma10 decline avoided %    over the declines of 20% or more from the running peak (peak to
#                            trough, one still under way included), the share of each decline's
#                            log fall the rule was out for, averaged over the declines
# sma10 false-exit return %  the index's cumulative return over each FALSE exit -- an out-period
#                            no month of which lies in a decline's peak-to-trough window --
# sma10 exits per year       the out-periods (maximal runs of months out) a year
# market sign12 trend %/mo   the index's mean next-month return after a positive trailing twelve
#                            months less after a negative one
# Graded by where the record falls among the world's single histories of the timing window's
# length, inside the four rows' joint band at 0.05: a one-year block resample keeps no decline
# whole. Each set grades its own index's record (2026-10-03): the S&P CRSP's century, the Nasdaq
# the IXIC+NDX splice over 1971-2026 (56 years). The Nasdaq's CRSP and NDX rows are reported, not
# graded: CRSP is another index, and the consumer's rules were selected on the NDX from 1990.
# `Anchors.timing` are the graded series' records, `NASDAQ_REPORTED` the reported ones'.
# MONTH-END levels, as the model's are. Shiller's monthly S&P is a monthly AVERAGE of daily
# prices, which smooths the rule's signal and overstates the index's persistence at short lags:
# on the same CRSP series over 1926-2026 the averages read the false-exit return 4.0% against the
# month ends' 5.8% and 0.55 exits a year against 0.75, the avoided share 65.5 against 64.7; Shiller's
#   CRSP      Ken French's F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily (202606): Mkt-RF + RF compounded from the
#             window's first session, the level at each calendar month's last session;
#   IXIC+NDX  the Nasdaq Composite's daily log returns through 1985-10-01, the Nasdaq-100's after
#             (Yahoo Finance's ^IXIC and ^NDX closes), summed from 1971-02-08, the level at each
#             calendar month's last session; 1971-02..2026-09 (the last month to the 18th), 668
#   NDX       the Nasdaq-100's alone, the same way, 1990-01..2026-09, 441 months.
